mbpp_0793.reference_description: Write a java function to find the last position of an element in a sorted array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the last position of an element in a sorted array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Binary search for last occurrence in a sorted array

Main goal: The code defines a static method last that uses binary search to find the last index of a given target value within the first IIlIlllllllllll elements of the sorted int array IllIlllllllllll, returning -1 if the value is not present. As it searches, when it finds equal elements it records the index and continues to the right to locate the last occurrence.

mbpp_0953.reference_description: Write a java function to find the minimun number of subsets with distinct elements.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the minimun number of subsets with distinct elements.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Determine the maximum run length of identical values after sorting
Main goal: Sort the input integer array and compute the largest number of consecutive identical elements (i.e., the maximum frequency of any value). Note: The decompiled code contains artifacts (an unused void variable and an invalid return), so as written it wouldn’t compile; the intended logic is to return the maximum multiplicity of any element.

mbpp_0480.reference_description: Write a java function to find the maximum occurring character in a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the maximum occurring character in a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MaxOccurringChar - Most Frequent Character Detector
Main goal: Determine the character that occurs most frequently in a given string by building a frequency table and selecting the maximum.
Notes: The code counts character frequencies in an int[256] array (ASCII-limited), then finds the character with the highest count. It contains decompiler artifacts and a bug in the return statement (returns an unrelated variable) and would fail for characters beyond the 0–255 range or due to the apparent decompilation errors.

mbpp_0004.reference_description: Write a function to find the largest integers from a given array of numbers using heap queue algorithm.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the largest integers from a given array of numbers using heap queue algorithm.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: HeapQueueLargest - Top-k largest integers via a min-heap

Main goal: Given a list of integers and an integer k, return a list containing the k largest numbers from the input in descending order. It uses a PriorityQueue as a min-heap to keep at most k elements while scanning the input, then converts the heap to a list and sorts it in reverse order. If k <= 0, it returns an empty list. (Note: the decompiled code has a bug where it returns an unused variable instead of the result.)

mbpp_0532.reference_description: Write a function to check if the two given strings are permutations of each other.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the two given strings are permutations of each other.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: PermutationChecker - Anagram/permutation tester
Main goal: Determine whether two input strings are permutations (anagrams) of each other. The static method checkPermutation first checks that the strings have the same length, then sorts the characters of both strings and compares the sorted arrays element by element, returning true if they match and false otherwise. The class also contains an unused variable in its constructor, likely a decompilation artifact.

mbpp_0030.reference_description: Write a java function to count all the substrings starting and ending with same characters.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count all the substrings starting and ending with same characters.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SubstringCounter - Count substrings with equal ends
Main goal: For a given input string, count all substrings whose first and last characters are equal (including substrings of length 1). It uses a helper checkEquality to compare the first and last characters and iterates over all possible substrings via nested loops in countSubstringWithEqualEnds. The constructor is effectively a no-op.

mbpp_0615.reference_description: Write a function to find average value of the numbers in a given tuple of tuples.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find average value of the numbers in a given tuple of tuples.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code defines a class with a static method averageTuple that computes the average of each column in a 2D double array. It iterates over columns, sums values across all rows for each column, and divides by the number of rows to produce a 1D array of per-column averages, returning an empty array if the input is empty. The decompiled snippet contains artifacts (like an undefined return value var3_3) that would prevent compilation, but the intended behavior is to return the computed column averages.

mbpp_0754.reference_description: Write a function to find common index elements from three arrays.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find common index elements from three arrays.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: CommonIndexExtractor - Index-wise equality across three lists

Main goal: Provide a utility method extractIndexList that, for three lists of the same type, iterates up to the smallest list size and collects elements from the first list at positions where all three lists have equal values (A[i] == B[i] == C[i]), using null-safe comparison (Objects.equals). The result is a List<T> of the matching elements. Note: The decompiled code ends with a return of an undefined variable (var3_3); the intended behavior is to return the collected list.

mbpp_0806.reference_description: Write a function to find maximum run of uppercase characters in the given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find maximum run of uppercase characters in the given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MaxRunUppercase (intended functionality)
Main goal: Determine the maximum number of consecutive uppercase letters in the given string. The code intends to track the current run length and the maximum run length while iterating characters, resetting on non-uppercase, but it contains decompilation-induced naming and logic errors that prevent correct compilation or result.

mbpp_0325.reference_description: Write a java function to find the minimum number of squares whose sum is equal to a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the minimum number of squares whose sum is equal to a given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Minimum number of perfect squares
Main goal: Return the smallest count of perfect square numbers that sum to a given integer n by recursively trying all squares ≤ n and taking the minimum of 1 + getMinSquares(n - square).

mbpp_0219.reference_description: Write a function to extract maximum and minimum k elements in the given tuple.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to extract maximum and minimum k elements in the given tuple.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: ExtractMinMax
Main goal: The extractMinMax method takes a list of integers and an integer k, sorts the list, and returns a new list containing the k smallest and k largest elements from the input (i.e., the elements at the start and end of the sorted list). The decompiled code appears to return a faulty variable, but the intended behavior is to return the collected min/max elements.

mbpp_0110.reference_description: Write a function to extract the ranges that are missing from the given array with the given start range and end range values.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to extract the ranges that are missing from the given array with the given start range and end range values.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: RangeExtractor - Missing Range Extraction
Main goal: Given a list of existing intervals [start, end] and a global start and end bound, compute and return the list of gaps (missing ranges) within the bounds that are not covered by the input intervals. The method iterates through the input ranges, detects gaps before each range, advances the current position accordingly, and collects any trailing gap up to the end bound.

mbpp_0042.reference_description: Write a java function to find the sum of repeated elements in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the sum of repeated elements in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
<Response>
Title: Sum of Duplicate Elements in an Array ( Decompiled Java )

Summary_description: The code aims to compute the sum of all elements in the input integer array that occur more than once. It builds a frequency map of values, then iterates again to add to a running total only those values whose frequency is greater than 1. In effect, the intended behavior is to return the sum of all duplicated values in the array. However, the snippet contains decompiler artifacts and invalid Java (e.g., a void variable declaration and returning it), so as-is it would not compile. The n parameter is unused, and the apparent logic relies on a HashMap<Integer, Integer> to track counts and then sum values with count > 1.
</Response>

mbpp_0617.reference_description: Write a function to check for the number of jumps required of given length to reach a point of form (d, 0) from origin in a 2d plane.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check for the number of jumps required of given length to reach a point of form (d, 0) from origin in a 2d plane.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Minimal jumps with two step sizes
Main goal: Compute a small, case-based estimate of the minimum number of jumps needed to reach a target distance using two possible jump lengths, with special handling for zero target, when the target equals the smaller length, or when the target is at least the larger length; otherwise it returns 2.

mbpp_0487.reference_description: Write a function to sort array of tuples in increasing order by the last element in each tuple.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort array of tuples in increasing order by the last element in each tuple.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: TupleSorter.sortTuples - In-place bubble sort of tuples by last element

Main goal: Sort a List of tuple-like arrays (T[]) in ascending order based on their last element, mutating the input list. Note: The method returns an uninitialized list variable (null), so it effectively returns null instead of the sorted list, indicating a bug. The code uses a bubble-sort approach and relies on the last element of each tuple being Comparable.

mbpp_0589.reference_description: Write a function to find perfect squares between two given numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find perfect squares between two given numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: PerfectSquares: A Java class with a static method perfectSquares(start, end) that returns a list of all perfect square numbers in the inclusive range [start, end]. It checks each number in the range by testing whether it equals i*i for some integer i.

mbpp_0338.reference_description: Write a java function to count the number of substrings with same first and last characters.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count the number of substrings with same first and last characters.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Summary_description:
Title: SubstringCounter
Main goal: Count all substrings of the input string whose first and last characters are equal by enumerating every substring with nested loops and checking its endpoints; returns the total count (time complexity ~ O(n^2)). The code uses a helper to compare the ends of a substring, though the snippet includes decompilation artifacts.

mbpp_0974.reference_description: Write a function to find the minimum total path sum in the given triangle.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the minimum total path sum in the given triangle.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Minimum Path Sum in a Triangle
Main goal: Compute the minimum path sum from the top to the bottom of a triangular list of lists, where from each element you can move to the element directly below or to the right on the next row. It uses a bottom-up dynamic programming approach: initialize a dp array with the bottom row, then iteratively update dp for each preceding row with dp[j] = grid[i][j] + min(dp[j], dp[j+1]); finally return dp[0].

mbpp_0023.reference_description: Write a java function to find the maximum sum of elements of array in array of arrays.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the maximum sum of elements of array in array of arrays.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Maximum Row Sum Calculator
Goal: Given a list of integer lists, compute and return the largest sum among all the inner lists (i.e., the maximum row sum). The code iterates each inner list, sums its elements, tracks the maximum, and returns it (though the decompiled version contains artifacts that would return an uninitialized value instead of the computed maximum).

mbpp_0967.reference_description: Write a java function to accept the strings which contains all vowels.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to accept the strings which contains all vowels.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: VowelChecker
Main goal: Check if the input string contains all five vowels (a, e, i, o, u) at least once, regardless of case; returns "accepted" if all five distinct vowels are present, otherwise "not accepted". It uses a HashSet to track the distinct vowels found.

mbpp_0701.reference_description: Write a function to find the equilibrium index of the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the equilibrium index of the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code defines a class Solution with a static method equilibriumIndex that finds the equilibrium index of an int array: the index where the sum of elements to the left equals the sum to the right. It first computes the total sum, then traverses the array maintaining a running left sum and checking if left sum equals the remaining right sum (total minus left minus current). It returns the index when found, otherwise -1. The constructor and variable names are obfuscated.

mbpp_0134.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the last element of given array is even or odd after performing an operation p times.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the last element of given array is even or odd after performing an operation p times.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: CheckLast - Prefix-sum parity checker with a mode switch

Main goal: Given an int array, a length N, and a mode flag, it sums the first N elements of the array. If the mode flag equals 1, it returns "ODD" when the sum is even and "EVEN" when the sum is odd (inverted parity). If the mode flag is not 1, it always returns "EVEN". The constructor appears non-functional due to decompilation.

mbpp_0311.reference_description: Write a java function to set the left most unset bit.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to set the left most unset bit.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: BitUtils.setLeftMostUnsetBit

Main goal: Given an integer, identify the most significant zero bit within the number’s current binary width and set that bit to 1. If the input already consists only of 1s (i.e., of the form 2^k - 1, like 0, 1, 3, 7, 15, ...), the method returns the input unchanged. The implementation (obfuscated due to decompilation) effectively scans bits from least to most significant to locate the highest-order zero bit and then ORs the number with that bit.

mbpp_0102.reference_description: Write a function to convert snake case string to camel case string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to convert snake case string to camel case string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Converts a snake_case input string to CamelCase/PascalCase by splitting on underscores, capitalizing the first letter of each non-empty segment and lowercasing the rest, while preserving underscores for empty segments (e.g., consecutive or leading underscores). The class also contains a decompilation artifact in the constructor.

mbpp_0286.reference_description: Write a function to find the largest sum of contiguous array in the modified array which is formed by repeating the given array k times.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the largest sum of contiguous array in the modified array which is formed by repeating the given array k times.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Repeated-prefix Kadane maximum subarray

Main goal: The function computes the maximum subarray sum of a sequence formed by repeating the first N elements of the input array (N = IllIlllllllllll) a total of M = lIlIlllllllllll times, effectively concatenating the first N elements N×M times and applying Kadane’s algorithm to find the best contiguous sum. The code tracks a running sum and the maximum seen, resetting when the running sum becomes negative. (Note: decompilation artifacts make the return variable look invalid, but the intended result is the maximum subarray sum.)

mbpp_0355.reference_description: Write a java function to count the number of rectangles in a circle of radius r.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count the number of rectangles in a circle of radius r.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: A Java class CountRectangles with a static method countRectangles(n) that counts how many pairs of positive integers (a, b) with 1 ≤ a, b < 2n satisfy a^2 + b^2 ≤ (2n)^2. In effect, it counts lattice points in the first quadrant inside or on a circle of radius 2n, returning that count. The surrounding constructor and distorted variable names indicate decompiled/obfuscated code.

mbpp_0442.reference_description: Write a function to find the ration of positive numbers in an array of integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the ration of positive numbers in an array of integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: A Java class PositiveCounter with a static method positiveCount that returns the proportion of positive integers in the input array. It counts elements greater than zero, divides by the array length, and returns the result rounded to two decimal places (0.0 if the array is empty). The constructor contains an unused local variable, and the code uses obfuscated variable names.

mbpp_0350.reference_description: Write a java function to minimize the length of the string by removing occurrence of only one character.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to minimize the length of the string by removing occurrence of only one character.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MinimumLength - remove the most frequent character

Main goal: For a given lowercase string, count frequencies of each letter, find the maximum frequency, and return the original length minus that maximum. This yields the minimum possible remaining length if you delete all occurrences of the most frequent character.

Notes: The class mostly contains an obfuscated, effectively unused constructor; the functional logic resides in the static minimumLength method, which builds a 26-length frequency array, computes the max frequency, and returns length - maxFrequency.

mbpp_0411.reference_description: Write a function to convert the given snake case string to camel case string by using regex.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to convert the given snake case string to camel case string by using regex.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
A small Java utility class named StringUtils containing a method intended to convert snake_case strings to CamelCase. The static method snakeToCamel splits the input on underscores, capitalizes the first character of each non-empty segment, appends the rest of the segment when present, and concatenates the results. It also preserves underscores for empty segments (e.g., consecutive underscores). Example: "hello_world" -> "HelloWorld"; "a__b" -> "A_B". The constructor is meaningless boilerplate.

Note: The snippet shown contains decompiler artifacts and a bug where it returns a void/reference instead of the built string; the intended return should be the StringBuilder’s contents (IllIlllllllllll.toString()). In its current form, it would not compile.

mbpp_0650.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the given two arrays are equal or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the given two arrays are equal or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Equality check for two int arrays (after sorting)
Main goal: Determine if two int arrays have the same length and contain the same elements with the same multiplicities by sorting both arrays and comparing corresponding elements; returns true if they are identical, false otherwise. Note: the comparison loop uses IllIlllllllllll - 1, which omits the last element, introducing an off-by-one bug.

mbpp_0575.reference_description: Write a java function to find nth number in a sequence which is not a multiple of a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find nth number in a sequence which is not a multiple of a given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: A small utility class named SequenceCounter with a static method countNo(start, end, divisor, maxCount) that iterates through the inclusive range [start, end] and counts how many numbers are not divisible by divisor, stopping early when the count reaches maxCount, and returning the final count. The code is decompiled/obfuscated (odd constructor and variable names).

mbpp_0605.reference_description: Write a function to check if the given integer is a prime number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the given integer is a prime number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: PrimeChecker - Broken prime test
Main goal: A class intended to provide a primality tester via primeNum(int n), but the logic is flawed: it only checks divisibility by 2 for numbers greater than 4, causing most odd numbers to be treated as prime while many composites (e.g., 9, 15) are incorrectly labeled prime and true primes like 2, 3, and 5 are returned as non-prime.

mbpp_0530.reference_description: Write a function to find the ration of negative numbers in an array of integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the ration of negative numbers in an array of integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: NegativeCounter
Main goal: Computes the fraction of negative numbers in a given int array and returns that ratio as a double rounded to two decimals; returns 0.0 if the array is empty. The class includes a constructor with an unused local variable, likely an artifact of decompilation.

mbpp_0828.reference_description: Write a function to count alphabets,digits and special charactes in a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count alphabets,digits and special charactes in a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Counter class with character-type counting
Main goal: Provide a static method countAlphaDigSpl that iterates over a string, counts how many characters are letters, digits, and other characters, and returns these three counts in an int array. The loop increments the appropriate counter for each character and returns [letters, digits, others]. Note: the decompiled snippet includes artifacts and a no-op constructor, so the exact variable names and syntax aren’t valid, but the intended behavior is as described.

mbpp_0657.reference_description: Write a java function to find the first digit in factorial of a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the first digit in factorial of a given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: FactorialFirstDigit - Leading digit of n!

Main goal: The code intends to compute the first (leading) digit of n! (the factorial) by constructing n! with BigInteger, removing trailing zeros after each multiplication (i.e., removing factors of 10), and finally reducing the result to its most significant digit (dividing by 10 until only one digit remains) and returning that digit as an int. Note: the decompiled code contains artifacts (odd constructor, variable names, and a bogus void declaration) but the static method firstDigit implements the described logic.

mbpp_0047.reference_description: Write a java function to find the last digit when factorial of a divides factorial of b.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the last digit when factorial of a divides factorial of b.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: FactorialLastDigit
Main goal: Given two integers a and b, compute the last decimal digit of the product of the consecutive integers in the interval (a to b) with shortcuts: if a == b return 1, if the range is large (difference >= 5) return 0, otherwise multiply the factors' least significant digits modulo 10 to obtain the final digit.

mbpp_0757.reference_description: Write a function to count the pairs of reverse strings in the given string array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count the pairs of reverse strings in the given string array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Reverse String Reverse-Pair Counter

Main goal: Given a list of strings, count how many reverse-string matches exist by, for each element s[i], counting how many elements s[j] with j >= i equal reverse(s[i]); return the total as a string. Note: the decompiled code contains artifacts (e.g., a bogus void declaration) and would not compile, but conceptually it counts reverse pairs (including palindromes counted with themselves due to the inner loop starting at i).

mbpp_0225.reference_description: Write a java function to find the minimum element in a sorted and rotated array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the minimum element in a sorted and rotated array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Find minimum in rotated sorted array using binary search
Main goal: Implement a binary search to locate and return the smallest element in a rotated sorted array by repeatedly comparing the middle and rightmost elements and narrowing the search interval.

mbpp_0357.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum element of all the given tuple records.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum element of all the given tuple records.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code intends to compute the maximum integer value hidden inside a 2D list of strings (List<List<String>>). It iterates all inner strings, parses them as ints, and tracks the largest value, returning it. The decompiled snippet includes obfuscated/invalid artifacts (e.g., a void declaration and an incorrect return), but the intended behavior is to return the maximum integer found among all string representations.

mbpp_0351.reference_description: Write a java function to find the first element occurring k times in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the first element occurring k times in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Frequency-based first-element finder in a prefix
Main goal: Given an int array, a length n, and a target frequency k, count how many times each value appears in the first n elements, then return the first element among those n whose frequency equals k; if no such element exists, return -1. It uses a HashMap to tally counts. The constructor is unused/no-op.

mbpp_0096.reference_description: Write a java function to find the number of divisors of a given integer.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the number of divisors of a given integer.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Divisor Class and Buggy divisor Method
Main goal: Intended to count the number of divisors of a given integer, but the implementation is broken due to decompilation artifacts; it loops to count divisors inside, overwrites the count each iteration, and returns an uninitialized value, so it does not produce a valid result. The constructor is effectively a no-op.

mbpp_0414.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the value exists in a sequence or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the value exists in a sequence or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Goal: Determine if two lists share any common element. The overlapping() method brute-forces a check by comparing each element of the first list with each element of the second list using equals, returning 1 if a match is found and 0 otherwise. It runs in O(n*m) time and may throw NullPointerException if an element in the first list is null; the constructor contains an unused local variable and has no effect.

mbpp_0489.reference_description: Write a java function to find the frequency of the largest value in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the frequency of the largest value in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Frequency of the largest value in an array (obfuscated)
Main goal: Determine how many times the maximum element appears in the given integer array by a single pass, updating the max and its count as you iterate; returns the count. Note: the decompiled code contains issues (e.g., an invalid void variable and a broken return), so it isn't functioning as shown.

mbpp_0384.reference_description: Write a java function to find the frequency of the smallest value in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the frequency of the smallest value in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Frequency of the smallest element in an array
Main goal: Given a length n and an integer array, determine how many times the smallest value appears in the array. The code scans the array to track the current minimum and its frequency, resetting the count when a new minimum is found and incrementing when the same minimum is encountered; it should return the final count. Note: the decompiled snippet shows an invalid return (var3_3) but the intended result is the frequency count of the minimum value.

mbpp_0505.reference_description: Write a function to move all zeroes to the end of the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to move all zeroes to the end of the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: This code tries to move all non-zero elements of the input array to the front (preserving their original order) and fill the remaining positions with zeros, effectively reordering the array in place. However, the method returns an uninitialized local array (nArray), which would cause a compilation error; if fixed to return the input array, it would perform the described in-place reordering.

mbpp_0546.reference_description: Write a function to find the last occurrence of a character in a string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the last occurrence of a character in a string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: LastOccurrence - Find last occurrence index of a character
Main goal: Provide a static method lastOccurrenceChar that returns the index (as an Integer) of the last occurrence of a given character in a string, or null if the character does not occur. Note: The constructor and some variables appear to be artifacts of decompilation; the core logic is a linear scan that tracks the last matching index.

mbpp_0559.reference_description: Write a function to find the largest sum of contiguous subarray in the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the largest sum of contiguous subarray in the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MaxSubArray - Kadane's Algorithm
Main goal: Compute the maximum sum of any contiguous subarray within a given integer array (maximum subarray sum) using Kadane's algorithm; the decompiled code shows artifacts (e.g., invalid void variable) but the intended logic is to track the best sum while scanning the array.

mbpp_0557.reference_description: Write a function to toggle characters case in a string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to toggle characters case in a string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: StringUtils.toggleString
Main goal: Return a new string where each alphabetic character has its case swapped (uppercase becomes lowercase and vice versa); non-letter characters remain unchanged.

mbpp_0627.reference_description: Write a java function to find the smallest missing number from the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the smallest missing number from the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Binary search-based first-missing element finder
Main goal: To locate the smallest missing non-negative integer in a sorted array using a binary search strategy: compare the middle element with its index and recurse left or right, returning the appropriate boundary when a mismatch is found.

mbpp_0903.reference_description: Write a java function to count the total unset bits from 1 to n.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count the total unset bits from 1 to n.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: BitUtils - Count unset (zero) bits from 1 to n

Main goal: Provide a static method countUnsetBits(int n) that attempts to count the total number of 0 bits present in the binary representations of all integers from 1 to n (inclusive). It does this by iterating each number i from 1 to n and, for each i, repeatedly dividing by 2 and counting a zero bit whenever the current least significant bit is 0. mbpp_0969.reference_description: Write a function to join the tuples if they have similar initial elements.

The code appears decompiled with obfuscated variable names.

mbpp_0025.reference_description: Write a java function to find the product of non-repeated elements in a given array.

Note: the decompiled code contains several naming and indexing issues that would prevent compilation or correct execution (e.g., suspicious first-iteration indexing and unclear temporary variable usage), but the intended goal is to multiply all unique elements of the array.

mbpp_0125.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum difference between the number of 0s and number of 1s in any sub-string of the given binary string.

mbpp_0111.reference_description: Write a function to find common elements in given nested arrays. * array item * array item * array item * array item

mbpp_0101.reference_description: Write a function to find the kth element in the given array.

mbpp_0147.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum total path sum in the given triangle.

The code mutates the input array in place and should return the updated top element, though it contains a bug where it returns an uninitialized variable instead of the updated [0][0].

- Otherwise, returns true if (target - start) is a non-zero multiple of step and has the same sign as step; false otherwise.

- The method does not handle a zero step gracefully (will throw if step == 0).

mbpp_0464.reference_description: Write a function to check if all values are same in map.

The method iterates over map.values(), uses equals for comparison, and returns false on the first match (or null mismatch), otherwise returns true after checking all entries.

mbpp_0923.reference_description: Write a function to find the length of the shortest string that has both str1 and str2 as subsequences.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the length of the shortest string that has both str1 and str2 as subsequences.

It handles base cases when one substring is empty, uses a match condition on the last characters to recurse on the prefixes, and otherwise returns 1 plus the minimum of two recursive options to transform one string into the other.

mbpp_0891.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the given two numbers have same number of digits or not.

Description_Simple.comparison_text:

Main goal: Provide a static method sameLength(int a, int b) that returns true if both integers have the same number of decimal digits (including the case where both are zero) by repeatedly dividing each by 10 until they are exhausted; otherwise returns false. The constructor is a no-op, and the method does not robustly handle negative inputs.

mbpp_0521.reference_description: Write a function to print check if the triangle is scalene or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to print check if the triangle is scalene or not.

mbpp_0334.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the triangle is valid or not if sides are given.

mbpp_0148.reference_description: Write a function to divide a number into two parts such that the sum of digits is maximum.

Description_Simple.comparison_text:

Main goal: For a given positive long n, identify the largest number composed only of 9s (9, 99, 999, ...) that is <= n, call it p, and compute the sum of the digits of p plus the sum of the digits of (n - p). The code intends to implement:
- sumDigitsSingle: sum the decimal digits of a number.
- closest: construct the largest 9...9 number not exceeding the input.
- sumDigitsTwoParts: return sumDigitsSingle(p) + sumDigitsSingle(n - p) using the two helpers.

Notes: The decompiled code contains artifacts (e.g., unused void variables and incorrect returns) that would prevent compilation, but the intended logic is as described.

mbpp_0462.reference_description: Write a function to find all possible combinations of the elements of a given array.

mbpp_0255.reference_description: Write a function to choose specified number of colours from three different colours and generate all the combinations with repetitions.

Main goal: Given a list of strings (colors) and an integer k, generate all unique combinations of exactly k items from the list using a backtracking/depth-first approach, returning them as a list of lists of strings.

mbpp_0630.reference_description: Write a function to extract all the adjacent coordinates of the given coordinate tuple.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to extract all the adjacent coordinates of the given coordinate tuple.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Title: AdjacentCoordinates. The getCoordinates method initializes the process, and the private generate method recursively builds all combinations by exploring the -1..+1 range for each dimension and collecting completed coordinates.

mbpp_0540.reference_description: Write a java function to find the difference between highest and least frequencies in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the difference between highest and least frequencies in a given array.

The code appears obfuscated/decompiled, with some placeholder void declarations, but the intended behavior is to measure the gap between the largest and smallest lengths of consecutive duplicates.

mbpp_0445.reference_description: Write a function to perform index wise multiplication of tuple elements in the given two tuples.

Note: there is a bug — it returns an uninitialized variable (var2_2) instead of the computed result, so the function as written would fail to return the intended data. The odd variable names suggest the code was decompiled.

mbpp_0348.reference_description: Write a function to count sequences of given length having non-negative prefix sums that can be generated by given values.

The binCoff method computes C(n, k) with a multiplicative approach; findWays appears to return the central binomial coefficient C(n, n/2) but is broken by decompiler artifacts (invalid void usage and an erroneous division), so as written it won’t compile correctly.

mbpp_0259.reference_description: Write a function to maximize the given two tuples.

mbpp_0289.reference_description: Write a java function to calculate the number of odd days in a given year.

mbpp_0844.reference_description: Write a java function to find the kth element in an array containing odd elements first and then even elements.

The class constructor contains no meaningful logic beyond creating an unused local reference.

mbpp_0645.reference_description: Write a function to find the product of it’s kth index in the given tuples.

mbpp_0005.reference_description: Write a function to find the number of ways to fill it with 2 x 1 dominoes for the given 3 x n board.

mbpp_0164.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the sum of divisors are same or not.

The function maxSumSubseq initializes dp[0] = a[0], dp[1] = max(a[0], a[1]), and for i ≥ 2 updates dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + a[i], a[i]); it finally returns dp[n-1].

- f(0) = 0
- f(1) = 1
- For i from 2 to n: f(i) = max(i, f(i/2) + f(i/3) + f(i/4) + f(i/5))
The function returns f(n). Note: the decompiled code contains some artifacts (e.g., invalid declarations and an incorrect return) but the intended logic is the described DP solution.

Title: ToggleBits - utility to flip the end bits of an integer
Main goal: Provide two static helpers to identify and toggle the two boundary bits (the least significant set bit and the most significant set bit) of an integer.

Functions:
- takeLAndFSetBits(int x): Uses bit-twiddling to compute a mask equal to 2^p + 1, where p is the index of the highest set bit in x (i.e., 2^floor(log2(x))). For x = 0 it returns 1. This mask has 1s at the least significant bit (bit 0) and at the most significant set bit position.
- toggleFAndLBits(int n): If n == 1, returns 0 as a special case. Otherwise, returns n XOR takeLAndFSetBits(n), effectively toggling the two bits indicated by the mask (bit 0 and the most significant set bit) in n.

Other notes: The class includes a no-op constructor and appears to be decompiled code (the local variable usage in toggleFAndLBits suggests a decompilation artifact). The intended behavior is to toggle the lowest and highest set bits of the input.

How it works (high level):
- setMiddleBits(int x): constructs a mask that has 1s in the positions between bit 1 up to the bit before the most significant set bit of x. It uses a standard bit-propagation trick to fill all lower bits with 1s, then derives the mask via n >> 1 ^ 1.
- toggleMiddleBits(int n): if the input is 1, returns 1; otherwise returns n XOR setMiddleBits(n). This flips the middle bits of n according to the computed mask.

Note: The decompiled code shows an uninitialized variable in toggleMiddleBits, but the intended logic is to apply the mask derived from the input itself to flip the middle bits. The core idea is to toggle the middle region between MSB and LSB of the input.

Description_Simple.comparison_text: Converts a base-10 integer to its octal representation by repeatedly dividing by 8 and accumulating the remainders as decimal digits, effectively returning the octal value as a decimal-number composed of digits 0–7. The code appears obfuscated/decompiled and contains artifacts that would prevent compilation, but the intended function is decimal-to-octal conversion.

mbpp_0647.reference_description: Write a function to split a string at uppercase letters.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to split a string at uppercase letters.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Summary_description
Title: StringSplitter - Split PascalCase/CamelCase strings into words
Main goal: To take a string where each word starts with an uppercase letter and return a list of the individual words. It does this by using the regex "[A-Z][^A-Z]*" to find each segment that begins with an uppercase letter followed by non-uppercase characters, collecting them into a List<String>.

Notes: The provided snippet appears to be a decompiled artifact with intentional junk (e.g., void var1_1 and an invalid return), so as written it wouldn’t compile. The intended behavior is to return the collected word tokens.

mbpp_0670.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether a sequence of numbers has a decreasing trend or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether a sequence of numbers has a decreasing trend or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: TrendChecker - Ascending-order verification
Main goal: Determine if a given list of integers is already sorted in nondecreasing (ascending) order by comparing the original list to a sorted copy; returns true if they are equal. (The method named decreasingTrend actually checks for ascending order, and the constructor contains an unused local variable with no effect.)

mbpp_0734.reference_description: Write a java function to find sum of products of all possible subarrays.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find sum of products of all possible subarrays.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Sum of subarray products
Main goal: Given an integer array, compute the sum of the products of all contiguous subarrays using a dynamic accumulation (maintaining a running subarray-product sum and a total). The intended logic updates current = a[i] * (1 + prev), adds current to a running total, and sets prev = current; note that the decompiled code contains a bug (returning a void-typed variable) but describes the classic approach.

mbpp_0719.reference_description: Write a function that matches a string that has an a followed by zero or more b's.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function that matches a string that has an a followed by zero or more b's.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Main goal: A tiny regex helper. The class TextMatch defines a static method textMatch that compiles the regex "ab*?" and tests whether the input string contains a match. If a match is found it returns "Found a match!", otherwise "Not matched!". Given the pattern, it effectively matches an 'a' (since 'a' followed by zero or more 'b's with lazy quantifier can be just 'a'), so the method reports presence of an 'a' in the input. The rest of the code includes an unusual, unused constructor likely from decompilation.

mbpp_0950.reference_description: Write a function to display sign of the chinese zodiac for given year.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to display sign of the chinese zodiac for given year.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Goal: Map a year to its Chinese zodiac sign by computing an index from (year − 2000) modulo 12 (adjusted to be non-negative) and returning the corresponding sign from a 12-element array (Dragon, Snake, Horse, sheep, Monkey, Rooster, Dog, Pig, Rat, Ox, Tiger, Hare). In effect, year 2000 maps to Dragon, then cycles every 12 years. Note: the decompiled code contains artifacts (e.g., an invalid void variable, odd constructor, and some naming inconsistencies) that would prevent compilation; a clean version would fix these issues and use conventional names (Rabbit instead of Hare, Goat instead of Sheep).

mbpp_0024.reference_description: Write a function to convert the given binary number to its decimal equivalent.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to convert the given binary number to its decimal equivalent.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Converter class for binary-to-decimal conversion

Main goal: The static method binaryToDecimal intends to convert a number whose decimal digits represent a binary sequence (for example, 1011) into its decimal value by iterating through each digit, treating it as a bit, and accumulating bit * 2^position. The loop processes digits from least significant to most significant and sums the result. The surrounding code appears obfuscated or decompiled (odd constructor code, unusual variable names, and a bogus void declaration that would not compile), but the core goal is a standard binary (encoded as digits) to decimal conversion.

mbpp_0015.reference_description: Write a function to split a string at lowercase letters.

mbpp_0044.reference_description: Write a function that matches a word at the beginning of a string.

What it does: Compiles the pattern ^\w+, tests the input with a Matcher, and returns "Found a match!" if a match is found at the start; otherwise "Not matched!".
Notes: The code uses obfuscated variable names and may contain a compile-time issue where the if statement references a differently named variable. The regex anchors at the start, so it checks only the prefix, not the entire string (e.g., "abc123" matches, " abc" does not).

mbpp_0254.reference_description: Write a function to find all words starting with 'a' or 'e' in a given string.

The code builds a regex matcher, iterates matches, and aggregates them into a list. Note: the constructor is effectively a no-op, and the return statement in wordsAE appears to return an undefined variable, which would prevent compilation; the intended return is the collected list.

mbpp_0330.reference_description: Write a function to find all three, four, five characters long words in the given string by using regex.

mbpp_0151.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the given number is co-prime or not.

Functions:
- gcd(int a, int b): Intended to implement the Euclidean algorithm to compute gcd(a, b).
- isCoprime(int a, int b): Returns true if gcd(a, b) == 1 (i.e., a and b are coprime).
Note: The gcd method as shown contains a decompiler/artifact bug (returns an uninitialized variable), and the constructor contains an odd unused statement.

Note: the decompiled snippet contains artifacts and a bug (uninitialized void-like variable and a mismatched loop increment) that would prevent proper compilation; conceptually it performs the sum of cubes up to n.

mbpp_0566.reference_description: Write a function to get the sum of a non-negative integer.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to get the sum of a non-negative integer.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Goal: implement a recursive function to sum the decimal digits of an integer. The sumDigits method intends to return the last digit plus the sum of the rest, stopping at 0. However, the code has a bug: it uses an uninitialized local variable 'n' instead of the input parameter, so it won't compile; the constructor also contains an unused local variable.

mbpp_0514.reference_description: Write a function to find the summation of tuple elements in the given tuple array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the summation of tuple elements in the given tuple array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: SumElements provides a static method sumElements that takes an int[] and returns the sum of its elements by iterating and accumulating. The constructor is effectively a no-op and contains decompiler artifacts.

mbpp_0655.reference_description: Write a java function to find the sum of fifth power of n natural numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the sum of fifth power of n natural numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Sum of fifth powers from 1 to n (fifthPowerSum)
Main goal: Compute the sum of i^5 for i from 1 to N and return it as a long. The function iterates over 1..N, accumulates i^5 into a running total, and returns the result. The code appears to be a decompiled fragment with obfuscated variable names and a likely bug (returning a void-declared variable instead of the computed sum).

mbpp_0649.reference_description: Write a java function to calculate the sum of the numbers in array between the indices of a specified range.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to calculate the sum of the numbers in array between the indices of a specified range.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SumRangeList
Main goal: Provide a static method that sums a contiguous subrange of an int array (from index l to r, inclusive) and returns the total. The decompiled code uses obfuscated names and includes a stray void variable, but the intended behavior is to compute and return the sum of array elements within the specified range.

mbpp_0636.reference_description: Write a java function to check if roots of a quadratic equation are reciprocal of each other or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check if roots of a quadratic equation are reciprocal of each other or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Quadratic - Simple equality check
Main goal: Exposes a static method Check_Solution that returns "Yes" if the first and third integer arguments are equal, otherwise returns "No"; the second argument is ignored. The constructor contains a decompilation artifact and does not implement real quadratic logic.

mbpp_0640.reference_description: Write a function to remove the parenthesis area in a string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to remove the parenthesis area in a string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
<Summary_description>
Title: Utils.removeParenthesis utility

Main goal: Provide a static helper that, given a list of strings, takes the first string (if present) and returns a version with any substrings enclosed in parentheses removed (including the parentheses themselves, and an optional preceding space). If the list is empty, it returns null. Note: the constructor is a no-op and the method only processes the first element, not the entire list.

mbpp_0738.reference_description: Write a function to calculate the geometric sum of n-1.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to calculate the geometric sum of n-1.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: GeometricSum - Recursive geometric series calculator
Main goal: compute S(n) = sum_{k=0}^n (1/2)^k using a recursive static method geometricSum(int n), returning 0 for negative input. The code, as written, uses an uninitialized variable n instead of the parameter, causing a compile error; the constructor also contains an unused local variable.

mbpp_0704.reference_description: Write a function to calculate the harmonic sum of n-1.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to calculate the harmonic sum of n-1.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Recursive computation of the nth harmonic number
Main goal: Implement HarmonicSum.harmonicSum(n) to compute H_n = 1 + 1/2 + ... + 1/n using recursion (base: H_1 = 1; recursive: H_n = H_{n-1} + 1/n). The decompiled code appears flawed (uninitialized local variables and a dubious constructor) but its intended purpose is this recursive harmonic sum.

mbpp_0798.reference_description: Write a java function to find the sum of an array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the sum of an array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SumArray - sums integers in an array
Main goal: Define a class with a static _sum(int[]) method that iterates the input array, accumulates a total, and returns it as an int. The constructor and decompiled artifacts suggest a simple array-sum utility, though the shown code contains invalid constructs (e.g., a void variable and an unused self-reference) that would not compile.

mbpp_0746.reference_description: Write a function to find area of a sector.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find area of a sector.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: SectorAreaCalculator aims to compute the area of a circular sector given a radius and an angle in degrees using area = pi * r^2 * (angle/360). The decompiled code is broken: it uses an incorrect pi constant, returns null for angles >= 360, and uses uninitialized variables, so it won't function correctly as written.

mbpp_0820.reference_description: Write a function to check whether the given month number contains 28 days or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check whether the given month number contains 28 days or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: MonthChecker — Main goal: provide a simple check to see if a given integer represents February (2). The static method checkMonthnumNumber(int) returns true only when the input equals 2; the constructor is effectively a no-op with an unused local variable.

mbpp_0840.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the roots of a quadratic equation are numerically equal but opposite in sign or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the roots of a quadratic equation are numerically equal but opposite in sign or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: QuadraticCheck - zero-coefficient validator
Main goal: Provide a static method that returns "Yes" if the second argument is exactly 0.0 and "No" otherwise, effectively checking whether a quadratic coefficient is zero (i.e., the equation is not quadratic). The class constructor has no meaningful behavior.

mbpp_0817.reference_description: Write a function to find numbers divisible by m or n from array of numbers using lambda function.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find numbers divisible by m or n from array of numbers using lambda function.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Divisible
Main goal: A small utility class that filters a list of integers, returning those that are divisible by either of two supplied divisors via the static method divOfNums. The constructor is a no-op, and the code appears obfuscated; beware of potential division-by-zero if a divisor is zero.

mbpp_0813.reference_description: Write a function to find length of the string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find length of the string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Title: Obfuscated StringUtils.stringLength. Main goal: Provide a utility to compute the length of a string by iterating over its characters; however, the decompiled code contains artifacts (invalid void variable and incorrect return) that render it non-compilable in its current form.

mbpp_0904.reference_description: Write a function to return true if the given number is even else return false.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to return true if the given number is even else return false.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: NumberUtils - Even Number Checker
Main goal: Provide a utility with a static method evenNum(int) that returns true if the given integer is even (n % 2 == 0). The class also contains a trivial, effectively unused constructor, which is likely an artifact of decompiled code.

mbpp_0860.reference_description: Write a function to check whether the given string is ending with only alphanumeric characters or not using regex.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check whether the given string is ending with only alphanumeric characters or not using regex.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: End-with-Alphanumeric Check

Main goal: Provide a small utility that exposes checkAlphanumeric(String s), which returns "Accept" if the input string ends with an alphanumeric character (A–Z, a–z, or 0–9), and "Discard" otherwise. It uses the regex ".*[A-Za-z0-9]$" to enforce that the last character is alphanumeric. The class also contains an unused local variable in its (pseudo) constructor, which has no effect on behavior.

mbpp_0883.reference_description: Write a function to find numbers divisible by m and n from array of numbers using lambda function.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find numbers divisible by m and n from array of numbers using lambda function.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Filter a list to numbers divisible by two divisors
Main goal: The Utils.divOfNums method returns a new list containing only the elements from a given integer list that are divisible by both of two provided integers, using a Java Stream filter (x % a == 0 && x % b == 0) and collecting the results. An extra unused variable in the constructor appears to be a decompilation artifact.

mbpp_0871.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the given strings are rotations of each other or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the given strings are rotations of each other or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Determines whether one string is a rotation of another by concatenating the first string with itself and checking if the second string appears as a substring; returns false if their lengths differ. The decompiled code contains artifacts (odd variable names and a dummy void) but the intent is the standard rotation-check algorithm.

mbpp_0146.reference_description: Write a function to find the ascii value of total characters in a string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the ascii value of total characters in a string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: ASCII value of the first character

Main goal: The code defines a class Main with a static method asciiValueString(String). This method returns the integer code (the Unicode value) of the first character of the provided string if it is non-empty, and returns 0 if the string is empty. If the input is null, it would throw a NullPointerException. The constructor contains a pointless local variable declaration and has no meaningful effect.

mbpp_0925.reference_description: Write a java function to calculate the product of all the numbers of a given tuple.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to calculate the product of all the numbers of a given tuple.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: TupleProduct – A small utility class intended to compute the product of integers in an array. Main goal: the static method multiplyTuple(int[]) multiplies all elements of the input array (starting from 1) and returns the resulting product. The constructor and some odd decompiler artifacts (e.g., a void-typed local and a strange return) appear to be artifacts; the intended behavior is to return the product of all array elements.

mbpp_0915.reference_description: Write a function to rearrange positive and negative numbers in a given array using lambda function.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to rearrange positive and negative numbers in a given array using lambda function.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Rearranger - custom integer reordering using a reciprocal-based key
Main goal: Provide a static method rearrangeNumbs that returns a new list of integers sorted by a special key: map v to 0.0 if v == 0, else -1.0 / v. This results in positives coming first (in ascending order), then zeros, then negatives (in ascending order).

mbpp_0006.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the two numbers differ at one bit position only or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the two numbers differ at one bit position only or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: BitUtils - power-of-two checks and one-bit-difference detection
Main goal: Provide two static utilities: isPowerOfTwo(n) to check if an int is a power of two, and differAtOneBitPos(a, b) to check if two ints differ in exactly one bit by evaluating isPowerOfTwo(a ^ b).

mbpp_0211.reference_description: Write a java function to count numbers whose oth and nth bits are set.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count numbers whose oth and nth bits are set.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Summary_description:
Title: Broken Java snippet intended to compute a power-of-two count
Main goal: The method countNum is meant to return 1 when the input is 1, and otherwise return 2^(input-2). However, the code ignores the parameter and uses an uninitialized local variable, so it will not compile or run as is. The constructor also contains only an unused local variable, making the class effectively a no-op.

mbpp_0339.reference_description: Write a java function to find the maximum occuring divisor in an interval.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the maximum occuring divisor in an interval.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Placeholder divisor finder (stub)

Main goal: The code defines a class with a trivial, non-functional divisor-like method. The static method find_Divisor(int a, int b) returns b if a and b are equal; otherwise it returns 2. The constructor is effectively a no-op that declares an unused local variable. Overall, this is a skeleton/decompiled snippet with no real divisor computation.

mbpp_0173.reference_description: Write a function to remove everything except alphanumeric characters from a string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to remove everything except alphanumeric characters from a string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Goal: sanitize a string by removing all non-alphanumeric characters (and underscores) so that only letters and digits remain; returns null if input is null. Note: The implementation has a bug (it uses an undefined variable 'string' instead of the input) and the constructor is nonsensical, so the code as written is not compilable.

mbpp_0479.reference_description: Write a java function to find the first digit of a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the first digit of a given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: FirstDigitFinder – Leading digit extractor
Main goal: Provide a static method firstDigit(long) that returns the most significant (first) digit of the input by dividing out trailing digits until only one digit remains. Note: the snippet includes a bug where a local variable 'l' is declared but never assigned, causing the method to fail to return a value as written; a corrected version should return the final single-digit value (e.g., cast IIlllllllllllll after the loop or assign l accordingly). The constructor itself is a no-op.

mbpp_0924.reference_description: Write a function to find maximum of two numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find maximum of two numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MaxFinder - Max of Two Integers
Main goal: Provide a small utility that returns the larger of two int values via the static method maxOfTwo(int a, int b). The class also contains a skeletal constructor and decompilation artifacts (unused variables, a bogus void declaration, and an odd else-return), but the intended functionality is to compare the two inputs and return the greater one.

mbpp_0678.reference_description: Write a java function to remove spaces from a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to remove spaces from a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: RemoveSpaces utility
Main goal: Provide a static method removeSpaces that returns the given string with all space characters removed (null-safe). Note: The implementation as shown is broken (uses an uninitialized local variable 'string'), so it won't compile.

mbpp_0970.reference_description: Write a function to find minimum of two numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find minimum of two numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Title: minOfTwo - Goal: return the smaller of two integers (a min function). The decompiled code is broken (nonsensical constructor and an invalid void variable), so it won't compile as shown.

mbpp_0626.reference_description: Write a java function to find the largest triangle that can be inscribed in the semicircle.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the largest triangle that can be inscribed in the semicircle.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Triangle class with a flawed area method
Main goal: Intended to provide a triangleArea(double) that returns the square of the input for non-negative values and -1.0 if negative; however, the decompiled code uses an uninitialized local variable and a no-op constructor, so it cannot run as written.
